item.content:encoded: Nach der Investorenkonferenz der Bundesregierung in Berlin zeigt sich Kanzler Friedrich Merz zufrieden. "Wir sind entschlossen, Deutschland einen großen Schub zu geben." Es seien Investitionen im Umfang von rund 230 Milliarden Euro zugesagt worden, sagte der CDU-Chef am Dienstag zu Journalisten. Allein Amazon (AMZN.O) wolle 16 Milliarden Euro investieren. Weitere Zusagen kämen von den US-Technologiefirmen Nvidia (NVDA.O) und Microsoft (MSFT.O) , der für Lidl bekannten Schwarz-Gruppe, RWE (RWEG.DE) , Sanofi (SASY.PA) und dem US-Investor Blackstone (BX.N) . Merz sagte, die Regierung wolle mit Reformen dem Vertrauen gerecht werden und weitere Investorentreffen abhalten. Diese Veranstaltung solle nur der Anfang sein. Merz ergänzte, große Unterstützung habe er für die Reformen im Rentensystem bekommen. Hier soll ein größerer Teil der Rente künftig aus Investments am Kapitalmarkt kommen. "Wir machen aus einem Land der Sparer ein Land der Investoren." Ähnlich äußerte sich Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil. Die Frühstartrente, bei der der Staat jeden Monat zehn Euro für Kinder anlegen will, werde zu einem Kulturwandel führen. SPD-Chef Klingbeil sagte, der Blick auf Deutschland ändere sich gerade. "Es passiert was in Deutschland." Er verwies auf die Wachstumsprognosen von über einem Prozent in diesem und im nächsten Jahr. "Deutschland ist zurück." Die Regierung dürfe sich deswegen aber nicht zurücklehnen und müsse weitere Reformen angehen. Die klare Erwartung der Investoren sei gewesen, dass Deutschland dabei in Europa der Treiber sei. "Investitionen sind willkommen", sagte Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU). Sie sprach von imposanten Zusagen der Investoren. Es gebe aber einen harten Wettbewerb um Geldgeber. "Die Konkurrenz schläft nicht." Enteignungen, wie sie die wahrscheinliche Landesregierung in Berlin für große Immobilienkonzerne plant, seien Gift. Die Bundesregierung werde privates Eigentum schützen.

item.title: EU Commission weighs aligning worker posting, social-security procedures
item.description: The European Commission is examining ways to align procedures for worker postings and social-security certificates after the European Parliament approved a new EU-wide electronic declaration system, it told Reuters on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Cian Muenster
item.content:encoded: The European Commission is examining ways to align procedures for worker postings and social-security certificates after the European Parliament approved a new EU-wide electronic declaration system, it told Reuters on Tuesday. The Commission said it was assessing how the "once-only" principle could apply to both A1 social-security certificates and the new eDeclaration system for employees temporarily posted to another EU country, potentially reducing paperwork for companies operating across the bloc. "These two procedures could be brought closer together from both a technical and user-oriented perspective once the common eDeclaration portal for the posting of workers is in place," a Commission spokesperson said. Employers have long complained about the administrative burden associated with A1 certificates, which show that employees working temporarily abroad remain covered by their home country's social-security system. More than 5.6 million certificates were issued across Europe in 2024. The European Parliament approved legislation establishing the eDeclaration system for posted workers, which will create a common EU portal and standardised form for companies to notify authorities when temporarily sending employees to another member state. During a parliamentary debate ahead of the vote, co-rapporteur Johan Danielsson said the measure would cut red tape without weakening workers' rights. "I believe that the new portal for e-declaration of posted workers could be the example of how simplification can be achieved without deregulation," Danielsson said. Co-rapporteur Andreas Schwab called the proposal "a huge step towards simplification of posting of workers". The European Trade Union Confederation said the final legislation strengthened protections for workers and labour inspectors. Germany's VDMA engineering association welcomed the legislation but said it would deliver meaningful simplification only if a large number of EU countries participated. "If only a few countries make use of the voluntary procedure, the patchwork of differing reporting requirements across Europe will persist," a VDMA spokesperson said. The Commission declined to estimate how many member states were likely to participate, saying countries would have to notify Brussels at least six months before joining the system. It expects the platform to become operational in late 2027.

item.title: SONDEO Actividad económica de Argentina habría registrado mínima mejora en agosto
item.description: El Estimador Mensual de Actividad Económica (EMAE) de Argentina habría avanzado apenas un 0,3% interanual en el octavo mes del año, luego de la fuerte contracción anotada el mes anterior, según la mediana de un sondeo de Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Hernan Nessi
item.content:encoded: El Estimador Mensual de Actividad Económica (EMAE) de Argentina habría avanzado apenas un 0,3% interanual en el octavo mes del año, luego de la fuerte contracción anotada el mes anterior, según la mediana de un sondeo de Reuters. En julio, según datos del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), el EMAE registró un retroceso de 1,4% en su medición contra igual mes del año previo y una caída de 2,9% respecto de junio. Las proyecciones entre 15 analistas locales y extranjeros también reflejaron una mejora promedio de 0,4% para la actividad económica de agosto. Analistas consultados coinciden en que se mantiene la 'economía a dos velocidades', con sectores primarios que mejoran fuertemente y rubros relacionados al consumo que mantienen su denodada lucha por arrojar resultados positivos. "Se consolida la heterogeneidad con sectores que crecen fuerte, fundamentalmente transables primarios, y los asociados al consumo o a los centros urbanos con oscilaciones", dijo a Reuters Pablo Besmedrisnik, economista y director de VDC consultora. Y añadió que "el resultado es un crecimiento en forma de serrucho con una tendencia agregada de crecimiento limitado y lejos de los principales centros urbanos". La gran disparidad de estimaciones de los analistas encuestados oscilaron entre una contracción máxima de 0,8% y un avance tope de 3,3% para la variación interanual del EMAE de agosto. Las primeras proyecciones de los analistas para septiembre prevén que la actividad económica vuelva a anotar un resultado positivo. "Para septiembre los datos adelantados vienen bien por lo que esperamos que se encadenen dos meses positivos", expresó Diego Piccardo, economista jefe en la Fundación Libertad y Progreso. "Luego, el Gobierno apuesta a las concesiones de rutas, al crédito hipotecario y que los sectores dinámicos sigan traccionando para que la economía termine de arrancar y se sienta en 'la calle' antes de las elecciones" presidenciales del 2027, agregó. Analistas también proyectan que con los datos que arrojaría el EMAE en agosto y septiembre, la economía argentina difícilmente no caiga en recesión técnica. "El EMAE de julio cayó 2,9% mensual -1,4% negativo interanual-, la mayor contracción mensual desde la pandemia, y la mayor desde septiembre del 2019 excluyendo crisis 'COVID'", afirmó Juan Manuel Franco, economista del Grupo SBS. Y explicó que "con julio en baja, el tercer trimestre del 2026 arranca cuesta arriba y el escenario de recesión técnica pasó a ser consenso ya que se necesitaría en agosto y septiembre una suba de 5,7% directo para evitar la caída trimestral".

item.title: Protesto de caminhoneiros coloca em risco produção de massas na Itália
item.description: A produção de massas italianas está ameaçada por um protesto de caminhoneiros no sul do país, motivado pela alta nos preços dos combustíveis e do custo de vida, bloqueando as entregas às fábricas.
item.dc:creator: Sara Rossi
item.content:encoded: A produção de massas italianas está ameaçada por um protesto de caminhoneiros no sul do país, motivado pela alta nos preços dos combustíveis e do custo de vida, bloqueando as entregas às fábricas. A fabricante de massas Rummo, com sede na região de Campânia, no sul da Itália, informou nesta terça-feira que suspendeu a produção após ficar sem ingredientes. Quase todos os principais produtores de massas da região vizinha da Apúlia -- que, juntamente com a Campânia e a Sicília, forma o coração da produção de massas da Itália -- estão enfrentando dificuldades semelhantes, disse o presidente-executivo Cosimo Rummo ao jornal “La Repubblica”. “Isso significa que a maior parte da produção de massas da Itália está paralisada, ou está prestes a ficar”, afirmou. A La Molisana, outra fabricante sediada na região de Molise, informou nesta terça-feira que sofreu uma queda significativa na produção e foi forçada a recorrer aos seus estoques de matérias-primas, como trigo e sêmola. A Italmopa, associação italiana do setor de moagem, alertou na semana passada que um número crescente de fábricas poderia ser forçado a interromper a produção, com repercussões em toda a cadeia de abastecimento caso os protestos continuassem. A cadeia de abastecimento de massas da Itália gerou no ano passado 13,5 bilhões de euros em receitas, informou a European House-Ambrosetti (Grupo TEHA) em um relatório divulgado em setembro. ALIMENTOS E COMBUSTÍVEL ESTÃO SE ESGOTANDO O governo está prometendo mais ajuda para os transportadores rodoviários. Após se reunir com seus representantes nesta terça-feira, o vice-ministro de Infraestrutura, Edoardo Rixi, disse que um pacote no valor de mais de 150 milhões de euros seria disponibilizado em breve. Além disso, o governo da primeira-ministra Giorgia Meloni está preparando uma ofensiva de segurança em resposta aos distúrbios ocorridos no fim de semana em Milão e em outras cidades do norte, que surgiram no contexto de manifestações contra a inflação. O protesto dos caminhoneiros, que começou na semana passada com o bloqueio de estradas, rodovias e portos na Sicília e no sul, está causando perturbações generalizadas, incluindo escassez nos supermercados e filas nos postos de gasolina. “As pessoas tentavam pegar o que restava. Tive que ir a uma cidade vizinha e também estoquei farinha e os alimentos que mais consumimos”, disse Zineb Boutimah, 45 anos, que mora em Locri, uma cidade na província de Reggio Calabria, no sul do país. Elena Lombardo, 78 anos, também de Locri, disse que o frentista do posto de gasolina local a incentivou a encher o tanque na segunda-feira, alertando: “Não sei se haverá gasolina amanhã”. Nesta terça-feira, o posto de gasolina estava fechado.

item.title: Trump says in Kansas he does not plan to hurt Bombardier
item.description: President Donald Trump said late Monday he does not plan to hurt Canadian jet maker Bombardier more than a month after he threatened to bar them from the US market.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Allison Lampert
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said late Monday he does not plan to hurt Canadian jet maker Bombardier (BBDb.TO) more than a month after he threatened to bar them from the US market. Trump spoke in Wichita, Kansas, where Bombardier employs 1,500 workers. Trump's threats in September prompted calls to the White House from Kansas lawmakers including Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is facing a tough re-election bid. "I'm going to be helping a certain air company get themselves straightened away... I'll be helping them because I always viewed them as a Canadian company," Trump said. "But now I find out they have a presence here, and we're not hurting them if they're in Kansas. So we'll take care of those people and the jobs." Bombardier's shares rose 2.1% Tuesday after Trump's comments. The White House and Bombardier did not immediately comment. Bombardier has 3,500 jobs in the U.S., more than 40% of which are in Wichita, Kansas. Last week, Bombardier said it was investing another $50 million in its Wichita operations as part of its long-term growth plans in the state. Kansas is home to Bombardier Group’s US headquarters and Bombardier Defense. Bombardier has 3,500 employees in the United States and plans to open a facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Last month, the Trump administration banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import effective Sept. 29 but took no action against Bombardier. The action came after Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods took effect in early September which were prompted after Washington imposed tariffs on some $20 billion of Canadian goods in August, after several rounds of negotiations collapsed. Reuters reported last month it was not immediately clear how Trump could bar Bombardier private jets from being delivered to American customers since they have been approved by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. Threats by Trump in February to decertify Bombardier aircraft over a certification spat involving US rival Gulfstream Aerospace (GD.N) never materialized, with regulator Transport Canada eventually approving the American-made jets.

item.title: US FDA issues guidance on apps used with prescription drugs
item.description: The US FDA on Tuesday issued guidance aimed at clarifying how drug companies can develop, distribute and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US FDA on Tuesday issued guidance aimed at clarifying how drug companies can develop, distribute and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines. Here are some details: The policy outlines when content in such apps must be submitted to the US Food and Drug Administration, when those apps should be referenced in a drug's prescribing information, and what information companies need to provide to the health regulator. Apps linked to medical devices, such as software paired with an asthma inhaler, should generally be included in an associated drug's label, the FDA said Standalone apps that track symptoms, provide reminders or offer coaching should be listed in the label only if these apps are essential for the medicine's safe and effective use or offer meaningful clinical benefit, it said In most cases, information displayed to patients through a companion app will be treated as promotional material, in line with the regulator's approach to other forms of drug advertising The FDA said the guidance intends to reduce regulatory uncertainty for drugmakers and technology developers while maintaining safety and effectiveness standards

item.title: Regulador chileno investiga las pérdidas en fondos de pensiones de menor riesgo
item.description: La Superintendencia de Pensiones de Chile dijo el martes que inició un procedimiento para perseguir sanciones contra las siete administradoras que operan en el país debido a las recientes pérdidas en sus fondos de menor riesgo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Superintendencia de Pensiones de Chile dijo el martes que inició un procedimiento para perseguir sanciones contra las siete administradoras que operan en el país debido a las recientes pérdidas en sus fondos de menor riesgo. Las Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFP) han sido objeto de duras críticas debido a una caída de más del 10% del fondo de menor riesgo entre enero y septiembre, atribuida al alza de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos, que provocó fuertes pérdidas en inversiones en derivados. El sistema privado de pensiones es operado por las AFP, que manejan cinco fondos de inversión que van desde el Fondo A, de más riesgo, hasta el conservador E, que está pensado para proteger los ahorros de quienes están prontos a jubilar. "Tras concluir todas las acciones de fiscalización respecto de las pérdidas de valor que han afectado particularmente a los Fondos de Pensiones Tipo D y E, decidió iniciar un proceso sancionatorio a cada una de las siete administradoras de fondos de pensiones (AFP) por su responsabilidad en las decisiones de inversión adoptadas", dijo en un comunicado. La medida busca determinar "si habrían incumplido o no" su función de "cautelar la obtención de una adecuada rentabilidad y seguridad en las inversiones". En un comunicado reciente tras conocerse las pérdidas, la Asociación de AFP de Chile trató de tranquilizar a los aportantes, afirmando que el rendimiento de los fondos de pensiones debe evaluarse en un largo plazo y no basarse en las fluctuaciones del mercado a corto plazo. La Asociación no respondió inmediatamente el martes a una solicitud de comentarios. En Chile operan Provida, Cuprum y Habitat de las estadounidenses Metlife, Principal y Prudential, respectivamente; Capital de la colombiana Sura, Vital de la italiana Generali, así como las locales Modelo y Uno. El actual sistema chileno privado de pensiones se puso en marcha en la década de 1980, durante la dictadura de Augusto Pinochet. El sistema lleva mucho tiempo bajo críticas por generar pensiones relativamente bajas, mientras que sus administradores obtienen sólidos beneficios. Tras años de debate político, el Congreso aprobó una importante reforma en 2025, cuya implantación comenzó por fases a partir de agosto del año pasado y se extenderá por varios años.

item.title: Ahead of elections, Bessent says a Democrat-led Congress could do little to stop Trump agenda
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that there was not much a Democrat-led House of Representatives could do to stop the Trump administration's agenda.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that there was not much a Democrat-led House of Representatives could do to stop the Trump administration's agenda. "I think there's very little," Bessent said in an interview on 2Way TV two weeks ahead of November's midterm elections. "We have very durable tariff authorities," he said, referring to Democrats' opposition to Trump broadly imposing tariffs on goods imported from countries around the world. Control of Congress is at stake as voters head to the polls on November 3 to choose members of the House of Representatives and Senate and governors in states across the country. The Republican Party currently has a narrow majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. The election comes as Trump's [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"approval rating"] has dipped over his handling of the high cost of living for Americans during the US-Israeli war with Iran that has raised fuel prices. Bessent said the Treasury's effort to isolate Iran economically was working. "We haven't seen any loadings at the Iranian oil facility on Kharg Island since August. Iran currently has no oil on the water," he said. "Panic is starting to set in ... I don't know whether it's going to take four more weeks or eight more weeks, but at a point, their economy will go nonlinear," he said. Bessent also said he had not heard whether Russian President Vladimir Putin had accepted Trump's invitation to attend the G20 summit in Florida in December. "I haven't seen his RSVP yea or nay yet," Bessent said. Trump has said Russia has agreed to supply diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war in Ukraine .

item.title: China says US' DeepSeek ban disregards Xi-Trump consensus
item.description: China's commerce ministry on Tuesday criticised a US government order banning Chinese AI model DeepSeek from federal agency IT systems, saying it harmed Chinese firms' interests and disregarded understandings reached by the countries' leaders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's commerce ministry on Tuesday criticised a US government [USN:L1N4650HF TEXT:"order banning"] Chinese AI model DeepSeek from federal agency IT systems, saying it harmed Chinese firms' interests and disregarded understandings reached by the countries' leaders. In a statement, the ministry urged the US to "immediately correct wrong practices ... and revoke relevant discriminatory restrictive measures," adding that Beijing would closely monitor developments and "take all necessary measures" to safeguard its interests. The US Homeland Security Department on Monday ordered the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services using the Chinese AI model from civilian federal agency IT systems. It also barred agencies from acquiring DeepSeek products or third-party services developed using the model. DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that their use could result in the transfer of sensitive data to China if used by US government employees or vendors. Beijing is "strongly dissatisfied and firmly opposes" the order, the commerce ministry said. China hopes the US will implement the consensus reached by the two leaders, work with China "in the same direction" and make full use of the China-US [USN:AZN4TK3M7 TEXT:"artificial intelligence dialogue"] mechanism, it added. In a separate statement on Tuesday, the ministry also voiced "firm opposition" against US sanctions on five Chinese entities over alleged AI trade secret theft. The companies sanctioned by the US State Department on Monday were Shanghai Zhisuan Technology — an AI firm founded by former Google software engineer Linwei Ding — a venture capital firm that funded Zhisuan as well as three related entities. Ding was [USN:L6N3YU1BO TEXT:"found guilty"] in January of stealing AI trade secrets from the US tech giant to benefit two Chinese companies, although his conviction was [USN:L6N44H17F TEXT:"partially overturned"] in August. The Chinese ministry accused the US of "hyping up the so-called 'trade secret theft' issue" and of smearing Chinese firms. The rapid development of AI firms in China is the result of long-term investment and a commitment to technological self-reliance and open cooperation, and has nothing to do with trade secret theft, Beijing said.

item.title: Flávio promete recriar benefício ao setor de eventos instituído na pandemia e encerrado por Lula
item.description: O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) prometeu em vídeo publicado em redes sociais nesta terça-feira restabelecer o Programa Emergencial de Retomada do Setor de Eventos (Perse) se vencer a eleição, afirmando que a medida valerá para as áreas de eventos, shows e turismo.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Caram
item.content:encoded: O candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) prometeu em vídeo publicado em redes sociais nesta terça-feira restabelecer o Programa Emergencial de Retomada do Setor de Eventos (Perse) se vencer a eleição, afirmando que a medida valerá para as áreas de eventos, shows e turismo. O programa foi originalmente criado durante a pandemia de Covid-19 para socorrer o setor e teve elevado custo fiscal, com empresas de diferentes setores conseguindo acessar o benefício, que se prolongou bem além do período emergencial. A gestão do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva conseguiu encerrar o programa após longa negociação com o Congresso Nacional sobre um plano de ajuste das contas públicas. De acordo com Flávio, o programa estimulará grandes e pequenos artistas e aquecerá a economia do país. “Onde tem eventos o comércio vende mais, o taxista e o uber faturam, os pequenos artistas prosperam e a economia gira”, disse na publicação. Em abril de 2024, o Congresso aprovou projeto do governo que estabeleceu o encerramento do programa de incentivo tributário para o setor de eventos quando atingisse um custo total de R$15 bilhões a partir daquele momento. A cifra foi alcançada em cerca de um ano e o Perse foi finalizado, com celebração de técnicos do governo. Após o anúncio de Flávio, duas fontes da equipe econômica do governo Lula disseram, sob condição de anonimato, que para além do custo elevado do Perse, o programa apresentava distorções e chegou a ser usado por empresas envolvidas em lavagem de dinheiro. "As operações Jogo de Sombras, Arena e Conto da Sorte apuraram uso de empresas de eventos para lavagem de dinheiro do jogo", disse uma delas em referência a operações policiais que miraram empresas de apostas online. Ainda em 2024, a Receita Federal também identificou mais de 2 mil empresas que usavam o incentivo fiscal sem que o Fisco tivesse registrado pedidos de habilitação para o benefício. Uma terceira fonte do governo destacou distorções no modelo do programa, que foi criado para socorrer empresas afetadas pelo fechamento de estabelecimentos comerciais durante a pandemia, mas teve como grande beneficiário o iFood, empresa que teve receitas fortemente multiplicadas durante a crise sanitária. Em 2025, a Reuters mostrou que o iFood pagou quase [USN:L1N3WC17R TEXT:"R$1 bilhão"] em tributos à Receita após o governo obter vitória na Justiça, que considerou indevido o uso dos benefícios do Perse. Na ocasião, a companhia argumentou que usufruiu do incentivo somente enquanto esteve vigente uma decisão judicial que a autorizava a fazê-lo.

item.title: Amazon to recruit over 300,000 workers for holiday season in first hiring jump in three years

item.title: Polish power regulator wants wider EU battery rule exceptions to ease grid struggle
item.description: Companies running Poland's local power grids should be allowed to own batteries where they are needed to stabilise the network, the head of the country's energy regulator told Reuters, calling for wider exceptions to the European Union's energy storage rules.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Gardawski, Marta Maciag
item.content:encoded: Companies running Poland's local power grids should be allowed to own batteries where they are needed to stabilise the network, the head of the country's energy regulator told Reuters, calling for wider exceptions to the European Union's energy storage rules. Storage should not be opened up to grid operators everywhere, only where it is required, said Renata Mroczek, the president of the Energy Regulatory Office (URE), talking to Reuters on the sidelines of the European Forum for New Ideas conference in Sopot on Friday. EU rules generally bar grid operators, which are funded by fees on consumers’ bills, from owning batteries, so they cannot use that money to compete with private investors. Poland allows exceptions only for batteries URE deems integral to the grid. Historically coal-reliant Poland’s power system is struggling to keep up with more than 1.6 million small solar installations, think tank Forum Energii said, as grid-ordered cuts to renewable output more than doubled in 2025 to nearly 1.4 terawatt-hours. "Without more storage and its flexibility, it will be very difficult, if not impossible, to lower prices," Mroczek said. Contracts for power to be delivered throughout 2027 averaged 556 zlotys ($142) per megawatt-hour in September, up from 448 zlotys in June, data from Polish Power Exchange showed, above the average of 495 zlotys in this year’s regulated household tariffs. State Assets Minister Wojciech Balczun said in September that the government had not ruled out freezing household electricity prices again next year, Polish media reported. Mroczek said past price freezes had not fostered competition or encouraged households to look for better offers from suppliers. ($1 = 3.9021 zlotys)

item.title: Ibovespa orbita 208 mil pontos com aval de estrangeiros na reta final da eleição
item.description: O Ibovespa avançava nesta terça-feira, orbitando os 208 mil pontos, com investidores em clima de expectativas para o desfecho da eleição presidencial no país, enquanto dados da B3 continuam mostrando fluxo de estrangeiros para as ações brasileiras.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa avançava nesta terça-feira, orbitando os 208 mil pontos, com investidores em clima de expectativas para o desfecho da eleição presidencial no país, enquanto dados da B3 continuam mostrando fluxo de estrangeiros para as ações brasileiras. Por volta de 11h10, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) , referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, subia 1,49%, a 208.135,09 pontos. O volume financeiro somava R$9,2 bilhões. "O Ibovespa está em tendência de alta e mantém a resistência em 209.700 pontos – máxima histórica. Caso supere esse nível, abrirá novamente o caminho para mais valorizações, em busca dos 220.000 pontos no curto prazo e dos 245.000 pontos no médio prazo", afirmaram analistas do Itaú BBA no relatório Diário do Grafista. Do lado da baixa, acrescentaram, o índice encontra suporte em 203.000 pontos. Eles avaliam que a ausência de uma direção definida pode ser a tônica dos próximos dias, "com o mercado em compasso de espera antes de buscar uma direção mais clara". Pesquisas eleitorais seguem mostrando um cenário apertado da disputa presidencial, mas com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ainda à frente numericamente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) nas últimas pesquisas para o segundo turno da eleição, no próximo dia 25. Em paralelo, dados atualizados da B3 mostravam saldo de capital externo positivo de R$20,99 bilhões em outubro até o dia 16, de R$18,75 bilhões até a véspera. No exterior, a terça-feira era negativa nos mercados acionários norte-americanos, mas havia alívio nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, com o yield do Treasury de 10 anos marcando 5,1105%, de 5,136% na véspera. DESTAQUES BTG PACTUAL UNIT subia 4,09%, melhor desempenho entre os bancos do Ibovespa, que têm se mostrado sensíveis às expectativas eleitorais. BRADESCO PN , que reporta balanço no final da quinta-feira, avançava 2,59%, ITAÚ UNIBANCO PN valorizava-se 2,05%, BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) tinha elevação de 0,71% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT mostrava acréscimo de 0,54%. PETROBRAS PN avançava 1,14% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) subia 0,9%. O Brasil ultrapassou a Arábia Saudita como o segundo maior [USN:L6N4660QF TEXT:"fornecedor"] de petróleo bruto para a China nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, segundo dados alfandegários divulgados pelo país asiático nesta terça-feira. VALE ON (VALE3.SA) recuava 0,92%, em linha com a fraqueza dos futuros do [USN:L6N4660RV TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China. MAGAZINE LUIZA ON (MGLU3.SA) disparava 6,76%, com o setor sensível a juros entre os destaques positivos em pregão com [USN:L1N4660J5 TEXT:"alívio"] na curva de juros brasileira. O amplo índice de consumo (.ICON) da B3 subia 2,79%. ÂNIMA EDUCAÇÃO ON (ANIM3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, perdia 6,54%, tendo como pano de fundo [USN:L1N465104 TEXT:"acordo"] da sua subsidiária de ensino de medicina Inspirali com o grupo de educação médica do Einstein para usar a marca do hospital em seus cursos a partir do próximo ano. O acordo de 20 anos envolve um pagamento fixo ao Einstein de R$150 milhões e pagamentos de 6% da receita líquida de novos alunos de medicina, entre outros detalhes. JSL ON (JSLG3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, avançava 7,64%, tendo no radar prévia de resultados mostrando [USN:S0N45000S TEXT:"receita bruta"] de R$3,09 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 5,9% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. AMERICANAS ON (AMER3.SA) , que não faz parte do Ibovespa, saltava 19,1%, após a Justiça do Rio de Janeiro decretar o [USN:L1N465112 TEXT:"encerramento"] do processo de recuperação judicial da companhia.

item.title: AstraZeneca-Amgen asthma drug hits 69% remission in esophageal disease trial
item.description: Amgen and AstraZeneca said on Tuesday their asthma drug helped reduce swallowing difficulties and achieved disease remission in 69% of patients with a type of chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amgen (AMGN.O) and AstraZeneca (AZN.L) said on Tuesday their asthma drug helped reduce swallowing difficulties and achieved disease remission in 69% of patients with a type of chronic inflammatory disorder of the esophagus. The result builds on August data, when AstraZeneca said the drug met the trial's main [USN:L6N44O0DF TEXT:"goals"] after 24 weeks of treatment by reducing esophageal inflammation and easing swallowing difficulties versus placebo. The drug Tezspire is being studied in patients with symptomatic and uncontrolled eosinophilic esophagitis, which causes swelling and irritation in the food pipe, making swallowing difficult and sometimes causing food to get stuck The monoclonal antibody blocks a protein called TSLP that drives the inflammatory pathway involved in both asthma and eosinophilic esophagitis About 65% on the 210 mg dose and 69% of patients on the 420 mg dose of the drug achieved remission of inflammation at 24 weeks, compared with 3.5% of patients on placebo The companies said the benefits were maintained through 52 weeks, with 67.8% of patients on the 210 mg dose and 63.3% on the 420 mg dose achieving disease remission, compared with 5.4% on placebo Tezspire reduced swallowing-difficulty scores by 18.8 points at the 210 mg dose and 22 points at the 420 mg dose after 24 weeks, compared with a 14.7-point reduction with placebo The most commonly reported side effects were upper respiratory infections, headache and diarrhea The drug is already approved in a number of countries as an add-on treatment for severe asthma and competes with Sanofi (SASY.PA) and Regeneron's (REGN.O) blockbuster drug Dupixent

item.title: Global warming is accelerating, leading climate scientist Rockström says
item.description: Global warming caused by fossil fuel emissions is accelerating, pushing many of the Earth's most important ecosystems close to their tipping points, said Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research.
item.dc:creator: Simon Jessop
item.content:encoded: Global warming caused by fossil fuel emissions is accelerating, pushing many of the Earth's most important ecosystems close to their tipping points, said Johan Rockström, director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. Speaking at the Reuters Sustainability Europe conference on Tuesday, Rockström said damage to coral reefs and the Amazon rainforest was close to becoming irreversible. Parts of the Atlantic Ocean circulation system, including the current that moderates Western Europe's climate with warm water from the Caribbean, were close to collapse. The latest science confirms the world is on course to exceed a 1.5 degree Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) rise in average surface temperature in the next few years, increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events , he said, ahead of the United Nations' [USN:L1N45U06N TEXT:"COP31"] climate talks starting on November 9. Companies looking to prepare and build resilience into their operations should treat climate and nature as a single integrated agenda rather than separate issues, he said. While prioritising efforts to decarbonise, they should also invest in helping preserve nature, particularly projects related to maintaining or rebuilding biodiversity and reserves of fresh water. Rockström said it was "incredibly disturbing" to see lobbying for an easing of rules on phasing out internal combustion engine vehicles, pointing to subsidies for petrol and diesel that were undermining consumer demand for electric vehicles.

item.title: US health agency confirms third measles-related death this year
item.description: A third person died due to measles in the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed on its website on Tuesday, as the country battles the largest measles outbreak in decades.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A third person died due to measles in the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed on its website on Tuesday, as the country battles the largest measles outbreak in decades. There were 4,410 confirmed cases of measles across the country as of October 15, according to the agency. It had reported [USN:L4N45L13A TEXT:"two deaths"] related to the once-eliminated disease in September. The agency has not disclosed the states in which the three deaths occurred. The US Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, told Reuters that the National Center for Health Statistics received another report of a measles-related death and verified that the disease was the underlying cause. Under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the CDC has drawn scrutiny for switching to NCHS mortality data to track measles deaths, replacing its earlier reliance on state health departments' figures. The CDC has said its death count could change as reviews are completed. The federal death toll remains lower than numbers reported by state officials. In Pennsylvania, the state hardest hit by the resurgence, local health authorities have reported at [USN:L4N45M1NB TEXT:"least five deaths"] linked to the disease this year. State officials are also reviewing an [USN:L4N45Y148 TEXT:"additional death"] reported by the Franklin County coroner. Pennsylvania has reported 1,286 cases as of October 19. Last week, the CDC said it would deploy [USN:L4N45Z1Q3 TEXT:"additional support to Pennsylvania"] to help investigate the ongoing measles outbreak after the state formally asked for federal aid through the agency's Epi-Aid emergency response program. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease but can be prevented through the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine, which is about 97% effective after two doses.

item.title: US single-family housing starts plunge; building permits hit 3-1/2-year low
item.description: US single-family homebuilding fell sharply in September and permits for future construction tumbled to a 3-1/2-year low as higher mortgage rates suppressed demand, suggesting residential investment resumed its declining trend in the third quarter.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US single-family homebuilding fell sharply in September and permits for future construction tumbled to a 3-1/2-year low as higher mortgage rates suppressed demand, suggesting residential investment resumed its declining trend in the third quarter. The report from the Commerce Department on Tuesday followed on the heels of a National Association of Home Builders survey on Monday showing sentiment among [USN:S0N44H00H TEXT:"single-family homebuilders"] plunged in October to the lowest level since June 2012. The deterioration in sentiment was blamed on rising material costs and mortgage rates as well as more expensive diesel and "worsening" labor conditions amid an immigration crackdown. Expensive mortgages have combined with still-elevated home prices to create what economists have called an affordability crisis, which is dominating campaign messaging ahead of the crucial November 3 [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. President Donald Trump earlier this year refused to sign a bipartisan housing affordability bill, calling it "a big yawn" as he pressed Congress, including fellow Republicans resisting his demands, to first pass separate and contentious voting requirements legislation. The housing bill became law without Trump's signature. "The weakness in housing starts is not surprising. Even if homebuilders were putting up new houses, who could afford to buy them?" said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "The housing market is about to go into a deep sleep unless Washington can do a 180 on its policies and make the cost of a new home more affordable." Single-family housing starts, which account for the bulk of homebuilding, dropped 4.6% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 859,000 units last month, the lowest level since September 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Homebuilding fell over the month in the South, Midwest and West regions, but increased in the Northeast. Single-family starts rose 2.6% on a year-on-year basis in September. Mortgage rates have surged in recent weeks, with the 30-year fixed rate averaging 7.40% last week, the highest level in nearly three years, data from mortgage finance firm Freddie Mac showed. The higher borrowing costs are tracking Treasury yields as the US-Israeli war with Iran [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"fans inflation"]. Slumping sales have led to a glut of unsold houses on the market, further reducing the incentive for developers to break ground on new single-family housing projects. Despite the overhang of new single-family homes, there is a national housing shortage, which is keeping home prices elevated. OIL PRICE SHOCK Single-family building permits decreased 4.0% to a rate of 845,000 units, the lowest level since March 2023. Permits fell in the Northeast, Midwest and South regions, but were unchanged in the West. They dropped 4.8% year-on-year in September. Residential investment rebounded in the second quarter, also reflecting renovations, making a small contribution to gross domestic product. The rise followed five straight quarterly declines. Some economists said construction workers were being pulled away from homebuilding to work on data centers. "Add to that uncertainty among both builders and buyers about inflation, and our best assessment is that starts will falter in the months ahead until the energy shock is better understood," said Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics. "So don’t bet on residential construction to recover anytime soon." But some economists viewed the slump in single-family homebuilding as necessary given the inventory bloat, with the NAHB survey also showing buyer traffic slumping in October to the lowest level since April 2012. "So, if builders just proceeded without making an adjustment, inventories would quickly back up," said Stephen Stanley, chief US economist at Santander US Capital Markets. "Hopefully, the slower pace of starts will prevent the market from getting too far out of balance." Starts for housing projects with five units or more, a very volatile segment, plummeted 7.2% to a rate of 349,000 units in September. Multifamily housing starts plunged 25.9% on a year-over-year basis. Overall housing starts decreased 5.2% to a pace of 1.221 million units. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast starts dropping to a rate of 1.305 million units. They declined 7.4% on a year-over-year basis in September. Building permits for multifamily housing projects increased 5.9% to a rate of 503,000 units last month. Overall building permits fell 0.2% to a rate of 1.400 million units. Economists had forecast permits falling to a rate of 1.395 million units. Permits dropped 3.0% on a year-over-year basis in September.

item.title: Kremlin says work is ongoing to ease humanitarian situation in Russian-controlled town of Oleshky
item.description: The Kremlin said on Tuesday that work was under way to ease the humanitarian situation in the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, where residents have reported a worsening food crisis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Kremlin said on Tuesday that work was under way to ease the humanitarian situation in the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, where residents have reported a [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"worsening food crisis"]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that President Vladimir Putin had discussed the situation in Oleshky with US President Donald Trump and told him that Russia's human rights commissioner was engaged on the issue. Putin told Pope Leo in a phone call on Friday that he [USN:S8N44A06B TEXT:"supported a Vatican initiative"] to help deliver supplies to civilians in Oleshky and was ready to cooperate on the matter. Russia and Ukraine both accuse each other of blocking supplies to the population of the town which Ukrainian forces want to retake.

item.title: El dólar cae por preocupaciones sobre la IA, el euro sube a pesar de disturbios en Francia
item.description: El dólar caía el martes al resurgir las dudas sobre el comercio relacionado con la inteligencia artificial, mientras que el euro subía levemente a pesar de las persistentes preocupaciones de los operadores por los disturbios en Francia.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El dólar caía el martes al resurgir las dudas sobre el comercio relacionado con la inteligencia artificial, mientras que el euro subía levemente a pesar de las persistentes preocupaciones de los operadores por los disturbios en Francia. * Las acciones de la empresa surcoreana de servicios de IA Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) se desplomaron un 32% en su debut en la bolsa de Seúl, una señal de que el sentimiento negativo hacia el sector de la IA en los mercados mundiales no está remitiendo. * Las fuertes entradas de capital en la bolsa estadounidense han respaldado al dólar. El aumento de las tasas de interés, impulsado en parte por las expectativas de crecimiento e inflación vinculadas al sector, también ha contribuido a ello. * El índice dólar , que mide la cotización de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas que incluye al yen y al euro, caía un 0,27% a 101,69, mientras que el euro subía un 0,2% a 1,1232 dólares. * Los operadores se mantenían cautelosos con respecto al euro a pesar de las modestas subidas del martes, ya que Francia se enfrenta a protestas generalizadas y a un panorama fiscal cada vez más sombrío. * El Gobierno dijo que los toques de queda nocturnos en las zonas afectadas por la violencia de las principales ciudades francesas habían supuesto un respiro frente a los peores disturbios que ha vivido el país en años. Se prevén más protestas para el fin de semana. * La libra esterlina se apreciaba un 0,66%, a 1,339 dólares, después de que los datos del mercado laboral mostraron un mercado laboral resistente, la última serie de datos del Reino Unido que sorprendió al alza. * Según datos de LSEG, los mercados están descontando casi por completo una subida de tasas de 25 puntos básicos por parte del Banco de Inglaterra en su próxima reunión, el 5 de noviembre. * El yen subía después de que una subasta de bonos del Estado japonés (JGB) a largo plazo registró una demanda récord. La moneda japonesa ganaba un 0,29% frente al dólar, a 158,04 unidades por dólar.

item.title: Salesforce deepens AI bets with $5.66 billion Braze deal
item.description: Salesforce said on Tuesday it would acquire Braze in a deal valued at about $5.66 billion, eyeing the New York-based company's AI-driven personalization tools to strengthen its business software offerings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Salesforce (CRM.N) said on Tuesday it would acquire Braze (BRZE.O) in a deal valued at about $5.66 billion, eyeing the New York-based company's AI-driven personalization tools to strengthen its business software offerings. The deal is the latest bet by Salesforce to accelerate its AI transition as investors worry that the rapid adoption of the technology could erode demand for traditional software. Braze Class A shareholders will receive $47.50 in cash per share held, representing a premium of about 58.1% to the stock's last close. Shares of Braze jumped more than 50% in early trading while Salesforce's stock dipped. Braze's AI tools help marketers optimize content, offers, channels and timing, and let brands send personalized messages to customers and respond to their behavior in real time. The company serves about 2,770 customers including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban Outfitters and Venmo. The transaction is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal year 2028, subject to required approvals. The company does not expect the deal to change its fiscal 2027 forecast. Salesforce has been doubling down on its AI offering and signed a $3.6 billion deal for [USN:L6N42N0XU TEXT:"AI agent platform Fin"] earlier this year and an $8 billion deal for [USN:L3N3RZ0OR TEXT:"Informatica"] last year. Salesforce would pay a $300 million termination fee, while Braze would pay $191.4 million if it abandons the deal. J.P. Morgan Securities is the exclusive financial adviser to Salesforce, while Qatalyst Partners is advising Braze.

item.title: Diesel russo retorna à Turquia e ao Brasil após fim de veto às exportações
item.description: Os carregamentos de diesel russo estão retornando aos seus destinos tradicionais depois que os Estados Unidos suspenderam as sanções e garantiram o fim da proibição de exportação, com pelo menos dois navios-tanque indicando viagens para a Turquia e o Brasil nos últimos dias, de acordo com dados de transporte marítimo da Kpler e da LSEG.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os carregamentos de diesel russo estão retornando aos seus destinos tradicionais depois que os Estados Unidos suspenderam as sanções e garantiram o fim da proibição de exportação, com pelo menos dois navios-tanque indicando viagens para a Turquia e o Brasil nos últimos dias, de acordo com dados de transporte marítimo da Kpler e da LSEG. A Rússia suspendeu, em 9 de outubro, a proibição autoimposta às exportações de diesel — introduzida para lidar com a escassez interna provocada por ataques de drones ucranianos a refinarias —, após fechar um acordo com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, para fornecer diesel aos mercados globais. O acordo incluiu o levantamento temporário das sanções dos EUA ao fornecimento de combustível russo, embora os embargos da UE e do Reino Unido às importações de combustível russo continuem em vigor. Trump está empenhado em tentar acalmar os preços do diesel antes das eleições de meio de mandato, em 3 de novembro. O diesel é um combustível essencial utilizado na indústria, na agricultura e no transporte. Normalmente o segundo maior exportador mundial de diesel, atrás apenas dos Estados Unidos, a Rússia já havia reduzido suas exportações no verão, antes de impor a proibição de exportação. EXPORTAÇÕES RUSSAS DE DIESEL CAÍRAM 41% ESTE ANO As exportações totais de diesel da Rússia ficaram em torno de 345.000 bpd neste ano até o momento, uma queda de 41% em relação ao ano passado, segundo os dados. O petroleiro Leruo indicava Manaus, no Brasil, como seu destino após partir do porto russo de Primorsk, no Mar Báltico, em 16 de outubro, segundo os dados. O petroleiro Dolunay, que partiu de Primorsk com uma carga de diesel em 14 de outubro, está a caminho de Alanya, na Turquia. Cada um dos dois petroleiros transporta cargas de 300.000 barris de diesel, segundo a Kpler. Marrocos também começou a importar diesel russo desde o fim da proibição de exportação. A Turquia recebeu cerca de 34% dos carregamentos de diesel russo neste ano até o momento, o Brasil 24% e Marrocos 10%, segundo dados da Kpler. “Com o retorno do abastecimento russo, as rotas comerciais estabelecidas são o destino mais lógico para esses barris inicialmente. Também espero que a Rússia priorize clientes que possam absorver volumes significativos rapidamente, em vez de perder tempo desenvolvendo novos mercados quando a disponibilidade global de diesel continua escassa”, disse a chefe de risco geopolítico da Kpler, Michelle Brouhard. Fornecedores turcos de combustível reduziram as compras de diesel de refinarias nacionais em antecipação ao recebimento das exportações russas, disseram à Reuters três fontes familiarizadas com o assunto. A Tupras e a Socar, que operam as principais refinarias da Turquia, não responderam a um pedido de comentário. RÚSSIA AFIRMA QUE PODE AUMENTAR DRASTICAMENTE AS EXPORTAÇÕES DE DIESEL Trump afirmou que a Rússia exportaria imediatamente 300 mil toneladas, ou 2,25 milhões de barris, seguidas por 500 mil toneladas em novembro e 1 milhão de toneladas “imediatamente depois”. O vice-primeiro-ministro Alexander Novak disse na semana passada que as exportações russas poderiam ultrapassar os níveis acordados com Trump, com meta de até 3,5 milhões de toneladas por mês (875.000 bpd) até o final do ano. Os volumes que Trump disse que a Rússia forneceria são modestos em comparação com o déficit global, mas, nos níveis discutidos por Novak, eles cobririam a maior parte da lacuna, afirmou o analista da Sparta Commodities, James Noel-Beswick. Os preços dos futuros de diesel de referência europeus não sofreram alterações significativas desde o acordo, de acordo com dados da LSEG, e eram negociados com um prêmio de US$80 em relação ao petróleo Brent nesta terça-feira. Esse valor ficou abaixo das máximas históricas de quase US$95 registradas no final de setembro, mas ainda é várias vezes superior ao de um ano atrás. Os embarques de diesel russo totalizaram cerca de 210 mil toneladas, ou 1,56 milhão de barris, entre 11 e 20 de outubro, segundo a Kpler.

item.title: Shark kills woman swimming off South Africa's Eastern Cape
item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed by a shark at a popular beach off the coast of South Africa's Eastern Cape province on Tuesday, local authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A 65-year-old woman was killed by a shark at a popular beach off the coast of South Africa's Eastern Cape province on Tuesday, local authorities said. "A fatal shark attack occurred at the Orient Beach this morning, resulting in a tragic loss of a swimmer," a spokesperson for the local municipality told Reuters. The woman was swimming with a group when she indicated she was in trouble, a witness told public broadcaster SABC. "We all realised she'd been bitten by a shark, and she was in a very bad way," the witness said. "The bites were very severe, but there were only two, one on her thigh and one on her upper arm." He said the woman was brought back to shore, where she was declared dead on the beach. Eastern Cape police said officers who attended the scene found her body with open wounds and opened an inquest. The species of shark involved was not immediately known. Buffalo City municipality has closed Orient Beach and nearby Eastern Beach until further notice and urged people to exercise caution. South Africa's coast has many shark species, but it is popularly known for great white sharks, which draw tourists worldwide for cage diving and shark-watching trips.

item.title: Russian diesel returns to Turkey, Brazil after export ban lifted, shipping data shows
item.description: Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG.
item.dc:creator: Robert Harvey, Enes Tunagur, Ahmad Ghaddar
item.content:encoded: Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG. Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on October 9 on diesel exports, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"striking a deal"] with US President Donald Trump to supply diesel to global markets. The deal included a temporary lifting of US sanctions on Russian fuel supply, though EU and UK embargoes on Russian fuel imports remain in force. Trump has set his sights on trying to calm diesel prices ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] on November 3. Diesel is a key fuel used in industry, agriculture and transportation. Usually the world's second-largest exporter of diesel after the United States, Russia had already reduced its exports in summer before imposing the export ban. RUSSIAN DIESEL EXPORTS DOWN 41% THIS YEAR Total Russian diesel exports were around 345,000 bpd over this year so far, down 41% from last year, the data show. The tanker Leruo was signalling Manaus, Brazil, as its destination after departing from Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk on October 16, the data showed. The tanker Dolunay, which departed Primorsk with a diesel cargo on October 14, is heading for Alanya, Turkey. The two tankers are each carrying 300,000-barrel diesel cargoes, according to Kpler. [USN:L6N4600IE TEXT:"Morocco"] has also begun importing Russian diesel since the lifting of the export ban. Turkey has received around 34% of Russian diesel loadings so far this year, Brazil 24% and Morocco 10%, according to Kpler data. ”With Russian supply returning, established trade routes are the most logical place for those barrels to go first. I would also expect Russia to prioritise customers that can absorb meaningful volumes quickly, rather than spend time developing new outlets when global diesel availability remains tight,” said Kpler’s head of geopolitical risk, Michelle Brouhard. Turkish fuel suppliers have reduced purchases of diesel from domestic refineries in anticipation of receiving Russian exports, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. Tupras and Socar, which operate Turkey’s major refineries, did not respond to a request for comment. RUSSIA SAYS IT COULD RAISE DIESEL EXPORTS SHARPLY Trump said Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter". Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said last week that [USN:L1N45Y0MF TEXT:"Russian exports could surpass "]the levels agreed with Trump, aiming for up to 3.5 million tons per month (875,000 bpd) by the end of the year. The volumes Trump said Russia would supply are modest in comparison to the global shortfall, but at the levels Novak discussed, they would close most of the gap, Sparta Commodities analyst James Noel-Beswick said. Prices of European benchmark diesel futures have not changed significantly since the deal, according to LSEG data, and were trading at an $80 premium to Brent crude on Tuesday. This was off all-time highs of almost $95 in late September, but still several times higher than a year ago. Russian diesel loadings totalled around 210,000 tons, or 1.56 million barrels, over October 11-20, according to Kpler.

item.title: Protesting truck drivers put Italy's pasta production at risk
item.description: The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories.
item.dc:creator: Sara Rossi, Francesca Piscioneri
item.content:encoded: The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories. There are also growing concerns about food supplies in Rome, as transport bottlenecks hamper deliveries from southern Italy to the capital. Italian agriculture lobby group Confagricoltura warned that producers in Sicily would have to destroy large quantities of perishable products if transportation did not resume. Pasta maker Rummo, based in the Campania region, said on Tuesday it had suspended production after running out of ingredients. Almost all major pasta producers in the neighbouring region of Puglia, which together with Campania and Sicily form the heartland of Italy's pasta production, are facing similar difficulties, CEO Cosimo Rummo told daily la Repubblica. "This means that most of Italy's pasta production has ground to a halt, or is close to," he said. La Molisana, another producer based in the Molise region, said it had experienced a significant drop in production and had been forced to draw on its stocks of raw materials such as wheat and semola flour. Italy's pasta supply chain last year generated €13.5 billion in revenue, the European House-Ambrosetti (TEHA Group) said in a report in September. The Centro Agroalimentare Roma (CAR), Italy's largest wholesale fruit and vegetable market, said roadblocks and higher transport costs were causing shortages of products such as tomatoes, peppers and grapes, pushing up prices and increasing reliance on imports from countries including Spain and Albania. FOOD AND PETROL RUNNING OUT IN SOUTHERN ITALY The government is pledging more aid for road hauliers. After meeting with their representatives on Tuesday, Deputy Infrastructure Minister Edoardo Rixi said a package worth more than €150 million would be made available soon. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration is also preparing [USN:L8N4660PD TEXT:"a security crackdown "]in response to weekend riots in Milan and other northern cities, which developed on the back of demonstrations against inflation. Vincenzo Aleccia, president of the Trapani trucking consortium in the western Sicilian port city, told Reuters that he knew the disruption was enormous but added that "it's a peaceful protest and it's for the benefit of the people," saying rising prices affected everyone. The protest, which began last week with the blocking of roads, motorways and ports in Sicily and the south, is causing shortages at supermarkets and queues at petrol stations. "People were trying to grab whatever was left. I had to go to a nearby town, and I also stocked up on flour and the food we consume most," said Zineb Boutimah, 45, who lives in Locri, a town in the southern province of Reggio Calabria. Elena Lombardo, 78, also from Locri, said her local petrol station attendant had urged her to fill up her tank on Monday, warning, "I don't know whether there will be any petrol tomorrow." On Tuesday, the petrol station was closed. ($1 = 0.8911 euros)

item.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
item.description: Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Qualcomm (QCOM.O) will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September. One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12% for the benchmark S&P 500 (.SPX) and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) . Qualcomm shares were up more than 1% after trading down about 0.5% earlier on Tuesday. In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit [USN:L6N43V1B5 TEXT:"below estimates"] and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."

item.title: Halliburton expects years-long oilfield demand from Gulf energy infrastructure rebuild
item.description: Halliburton forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, expecting efforts to restore energy production and rebuild inventories in the war-hit Middle East to support demand for oilfield equipment, even as North America remains subdued.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Mathur
item.content:encoded: Halliburton (HAL.N) forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, expecting efforts to restore energy production and rebuild inventories in the war-hit Middle East to support demand for oilfield equipment, even as North America remains subdued. Operating margins for the coming year will be about 15%, Chief Executive Jeff Miller said on Tuesday, an improvement of around 200 basis points. The forecast does not assume a recovery in US hydraulic fracturing activity. "This forecast includes a flat North America and no recovery in the domestic frac market, pointing to recovery in the Middle East and better margins post new contract start-ups abroad," said Citibank analyst Scott Gruber. Shares were up 2.4% after Halliburton beat third-quarter profit and revenue estimates. The US-Iran conflict, which is in its eighth month, has disrupted energy operations in the Middle East, delaying projects but potentially creating long-term demand for oilfield services. Consultancy Rystad Energy in April projected as much as $58 billion in repair costs for energy-linked infrastructure. "I expect the work to restore production, rebuild inventories and strengthen energy security will drive multi-year demand growth for oilfield services," Miller said. Quarterly revenue in the Middle East and Asia was broadly unchanged at $1.41 billion, Halliburton said. The company derives about a quarter of its total revenue from the Middle East. Revenue from the Middle East is expected to rise sequentially and year-over-year in the fourth quarter, Chief Operating Officer Shannon Slocum said on a post-earnings call. Outside the Middle East, international business is expected to grow about 12% this year, with Halliburton also anticipating solid growth in Venezuela, Slocum said. Oilfield service companies are rehiring workers and putting more equipment on the ground, as a US-backed multibillion-dollar plan to [USN:L6N46015P TEXT:"revive the country's battered"] oil industry gathers momentum. Latin America and Europe/Africa quarterly revenue rose 12.6% and 22.7%, respectively, in the third quarter, helping offset a 9% decline in North America due to weaker US pressure pumping activity. Total quarterly revenue rose 1.8% to $5.7 billion, topping analysts' estimates of $5.6 billion. Halliburton posted adjusted earnings of 60 cents per share for the three months ended September 30, beating analysts' average estimate of 58 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company expects fourth-quarter profit between 62 cents and 64 cents, compared with analysts' estimates of 64 cents.

item.title: Prudential sheds Brazil, Mexico units to CNP for $4 billion as it narrows its focus
item.description: Prudential Financial said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as part of its ongoing push to simplify its business.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prudential Financial (PRU.N) said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as part of its ongoing push to simplify its business. The deal adds momentum to Prudential's retreat from emerging markets — following divestitures in Indonesia, South Africa, and Kenya — as the US insurer sharpens focus on core businesses. In August, CEO Andy Sullivan said Prudential planned to slash the geographic footprint of its retirement and insurance businesses from more than a dozen countries to about half that number. Announcing the sale on Tuesday, Sullivan said, "We remain focused on narrowing our geographic footprint and building a simpler, more focused Prudential." The firm has operations in the United States, Asia, Europe and Latin America and roughly $1.6 trillion in assets as of June 30. Prudential will use the deal proceeds to invest in growth opportunities in retirement, asset management and select protection businesses in the US, Japan and select European markets. For CNP Assurances, the deal marks a major step in diversifying its Latin America business. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027. Morgan Stanley served as financial adviser to Prudential, while Goldman Sachs advised CNP Assurances.

item.title: GM shares sink as automaker signals rising cost pressures
item.description: General Motors' third-quarter core profit rose sharply on the back of strong pickup truck sales, but its shares fell on Tuesday after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall, Nathan Gomes
item.content:encoded: General Motors' (GM.N) third-quarter core profit rose sharply on the back of strong pickup truck sales, but its shares fell on Tuesday after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales. The company said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT), rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data. It tightened its annual adjusted earnings-per-share forecast to between $12.75 and $13.75, the midpoint of which is below analysts' estimates of $13.41, according to data compiled by LSEG. GM shares fell about 5% in morning trading. "We think the selloff primarily reflects disappointment with the fact that the midpoint of its updated guidance is below" Wall Street's consensus, CFRA analyst Garrett Nelson said in an investor note. GM expects the fourth quarter will be negatively affected by fewer truck deliveries as it prepares to launch redesigned versions of its Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, its biggest money makers. STOCK BUYBACK SHOWS CONFIDENCE IN '27 GM said commodity inflation, including higher expenses for logistics and computer chips, would total about $2 billion this year, the high end of its previous forecast. GM said it expects gross tariff costs will hit the lower end of a $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion forecast. For next year, the company said "the path forward is more challenging," but reiterated that it expects results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics. "The consumer has held up remarkably well. We should continue to watch it," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told analysts on the company’s conference call. "We haven't seen anything that indicates any weakness." But he said costs rose sharply over the last two months, specifically for steel, aluminum and logistics. He added that if commodity expenses don’t ease from recent levels, they could weigh on GM’s bottom line by $2 billion next year. JP Morgan said investors "are likely to question conviction for now" because of rising costs and uncertainty over whether the company can sustain its rich sales mix of pricey trucks. MORE TRUCKS, FEWER EVS BOOST PROFITS GM's board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results. In the third quarter, it sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The company has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration’s withdrawal of support for them. CFRA’s Nelson noted that GM has lost U.S. market share this year and blamed competition from hybrid vehicles, a category in which GM is essentially absent. The automaker in the past decade went all-in on electric vehicles, deciding against offering hybrid vehicles, which now represent more than 15% of US sales. "The company faces a tougher road ahead due to its lack of hybrid offerings," he said. Barra told analysts on a conference call that GM "will have hybrids", although she declined to cite a timeline or other details.

item.title: Hasbro raises annual revenue forecast on strong demand for digital games
item.description: Toymaker Hasbro raised full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business on Tuesday, as its flagship trading card game, "Magic: The Gathering", powers demand ahead of the crucial holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Mistry
item.content:encoded: Toymaker Hasbro (HAS.O) raised full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business on Tuesday, as its flagship trading card game, "Magic: The Gathering", powers demand ahead of the crucial holiday season. The Play-Doh maker has posted seven straight quarters of gains in digital gaming, which also includes Monopoly Go!, while stronger sales of collectibles linked to Marvel, K-Pop Demon Hunters and Transformers boosted demand for traditional toys. Its shares were up 5%. The Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment, the company's second-largest revenue generator, grew 31% during the third quarter. Revenue from the consumer products segment rose 4%. Quarterly revenue from "Magic: The Gathering" gaming franchise topped $600 million for the first time, up 34% from a year earlier, fueled by premiere sets — The Hobbit and Reality Fracture. Company executives now expect annual revenue in this segment to grow between 16% and 18%, versus the previous forecast of low double-digit range. "Hasbro's continued momentum is a sign that great play and collectible experiences remain top of mind for American consumers" despite inflationary pressures, said James Zahn, editor-in-chief at the Toy Book magazine. Hasbro expects fiscal 2026 revenue to grow in the range of 7% to 9% on constant currency basis, compared with its prior forecast a 5% to 7% rise. "We are continuing to see a pretty resilient consumer," Chief Financial Officer Gina Goetter said on a post-earnings call, adding the company enters the holiday season in good shape operationally. Hasbro has benefited from strategic partnerships and its investments in digital gaming and product innovation, while rival Mattel (MAT.O) faces investor pressure to better monetize its intellectual property. Quarterly revenue of Hasbro, which also doubled its share repurchase target for the year to about $400 million, stood at $1.60 billion. That beat analysts' average estimate of $1.48 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Adjusted profit per share of $2.90 also beat the estimate of $1.86. The company's results included about $55 million of tariff refunds.

item.title: TSX rises as easing oil prices, bond yields boost sentiment
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, as broad-based gains on easing oil prices and bond yields outweighed losses in energy shares.
item.dc:creator: Anand R
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, as broad-based gains on easing oil prices and bond yields outweighed losses in energy shares. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.64% at 36,160.04 points at 10:34 a.m. ET, with the energy sector (.SPTTEN) the only loser, down 1.6%.
